clue.text: How Texan for one speaks about a resignation

indicators.note: about means going around, so the drawl phrase is wrapped round the letter from 'a'

parts.note: a Texan speaks with a drawl, a slow drawn-out accent

explanation.surface: A Texan's slow way of talking is used to announce someone quitting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts A inside WITH DRAWL, between the W and the L of DRAWL.
explanation.definitionFit: Withdrawal can mean pulling out of a post or contest, the same as stepping down.

clue.text: Old politician's in top-level cover-up, some say

definitions.note: read as 'Old politician is', the 's standing for is

indicators.note: some say signals that the clue word is heard spoken rather than written

parts.note: a wig covers the top of the head

explanation.surface: A former politician is caught up in a scandal at the highest level.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some say' tells you the word is pronounced the same as WIG. The Whigs were the old British party that preceded the Liberals.
explanation.definitionFit: The Whigs were an eighteenth- and nineteenth-century British party, so a Whig is a politician of old.

clue.text: Poor food — change course

definitions.meaning: hardtack, or ..., is coarse ship's biscuit, food of poor quality
to turn a sailing boat onto a new heading

explanation.definitionFit: Tack means both rough basic fare and the sailing manoeuvre of turning into a new direction.

clue.text: How long have they offered rides on the beach?

definitions.text: How long have they offered rides on the beach?

parts.words: How long have they offered rides on the beach?
parts.note: seaside rides at British resorts are traditionally given by donkeys, so the question asks the length of their working lives, which reads as an idiom for a very long time

explanation.walkthrough: Donkey rides on the sand are a British seaside tradition; the phrase for an age of time fits the joke literally.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a very long time, which answers a question about how long something has gone on.

clue.text: Fruit needs bedding out, at length, now?

indicators.note: out means the bed word is taken away from the fruit

parts.note: an apricot is a fruit
a cot is a child's bed, here bedding

explanation.surface: Fruit plants need planting out in full now that spring is here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes COT from APRICOT, leaving APRI; 'at' just joins on L. The question mark marks 'now' as a date reference: the month the puzzle appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: The question mark allows the month of publication to stand for the present moment, a playful definition by example.

clue.text: One doesn't think of wildlife heartily eating fruit

indicators.note: eating means one piece takes the other inside it
heartily here means only the heart of the word is kept, its first and last letters dropped

parts.note: fauna is the animal life of a region
botanically a tomato is a fruit

explanation.surface: Someone who never thinks of animals tucks greedily into fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartily' keeps only the middle of the wildlife word, and 'eating' wraps that round the fruit; 'One doesn't think' describes a robot.
explanation.definitionFit: A robot acting mechanically without thought or will is an automaton.

clue.text: Covering crow's back

indicators.note: back means the word is read from end to start

parts.note: to crow is to boast or brag

explanation.surface: Something covering a crow's back, such as its feathers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns BRAG round; the 's is just a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Garb is clothing, which covers the body.

clue.text: For modelling, shape too is ideal

indicators.note: modelling means shaping clay anew, so the letters are reformed

explanation.surface: A sculptor's shape is held up as the ideal form.
explanation.definitionFit: An apotheosis is the perfect example or highest form of something, an ideal.

clue.text: Bachelor girl you will look up — no — progress there

parts.note: Linda is a girl's name

indicators.note: in a down clue, look up means read the word upwards, from end to start

parts.note: you will, archaically, is ye'll

explanation.surface: A single man is told to look up a girl, though it will get him nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'look up' reverses YE'LL to give LLEY.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead end, a road with no exit, is a place where no further progress is possible.

clue.text: Destroy, but retain nice fragments

indicators.note: fragments means broken into pieces, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Smash something up but keep the nice broken bits.
explanation.definitionFit: To incinerate is to burn something to ashes, destroying it completely.

clue.text: Beer ingredient discovered by one Indian

parts.note: hops flavour beer
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A brewing ingredient is first found by a person from India.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hopi are a Native American people of Arizona, an American Indian nation.

clue.text: Place the coil in alarm

parts.note: to place is to put
taken as written
to coil a spring is to wind it up

explanation.surface: Positioning a coiled spring makes someone jumpy.
explanation.definitionFit: To put the wind up someone is an idiom meaning to frighten or alarm them.

clue.text: Using euphemisms for spotty-faced?

definitions.meaning: speaking evasively and softening the truth
jokingly, having a speckled, meal-dusted mouth

explanation.definitionFit: Mealy-mouthed describes someone unwilling to speak plainly, while literally suggesting a speckled mouth.

clue.text: Ostentatious rooms in which chap keeps lad

indicators.note: in which says the rest goes inside the rooms word

parts.note: a flat is a set of rooms
a chap is a man
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A showy apartment where a man is looking after a boy.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest: 'keeps' sets the lad inside the chap, and 'in which' sets that pair inside the rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Flamboyant means showy and attention-seeking, the same as ostentatious.

clue.text: Moving scared down steps with much arm-waving

indicators.note: moving means the letters are shifted round into a new order

explanation.surface: A frightened person hurries downstairs, flailing their arms.
explanation.definitionFit: A Highland dance performed over crossed blades involves steps and raised arms, so it is steps with much arm-waving.

clue.text: Rarely the highest-rated resort?

parts.note: a resort that is often bottom of the table rather than top, the name split as 'lowest' plus the old word for often

explanation.walkthrough: The Suffolk seaside town splits as LOWEST + OFT, oft being poetic for often: a place often rated lowest.
explanation.definitionFit: Lowestoft is a seaside resort town on the Suffolk coast of eastern England.

clue.text: Won't you get here in the country?

definitions.text: Won't you get here in the country?

parts.words: Won't you get here in the country?
parts.note: going to the countryside takes you away from urban areas, so you end up somewhere beyond the city

explanation.definitionFit: Being in the countryside means being away from the urban centre, beyond the town limits.

clue.text: Cheerfully sing of monster fish

definitions.meaning: to sing in a carefree jolly way
an ugly creature of Scandinavian folklore
to fish by trailing a baited line behind a boat

explanation.definitionFit: Troll has three senses: to sing merrily, a folklore monster, and to fish with a trailing line.

clue.text: Lover of Homer has the edge, poetically

definitions.meaning: Homer Simpson's wife in the cartoon, not the Greek poet
a poetic word for a border or margin

explanation.definitionFit: Marge is Homer Simpson's wife, and also an archaic literary word for a margin.

clue.text: Point about strong emotion bringing colour

indicators.note: about means going around the emotion word

parts.note: a tine is a prong or point, as on a fork
anger is a strong emotion

explanation.surface: Making a point while worked up brings colour to the face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Point' looks like a verb but is a noun, the prong of a fork; 'about' wraps it round the emotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangerine is a deep orange shade, so it names a colour as well as a fruit.

clue.text: Valuable instruction in exclusive 'club

parts.note: an order is an instruction
of merit means having worth, valuable

explanation.surface: A useful rule laid down within a private members' club.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces appear in the clue in reverse: 'Valuable instruction' is an instruction of merit.
explanation.definitionFit: The Order of Merit is a British honour limited to a few members, a select society or exclusive club.

clue.text: Live up to verses she inspired

definitions.note: the muse is defined by what she inspired, lyric and love poetry

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read upwards, from end to start

parts.note: to live is to be, so 'are'
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone tries to match the poems their muse once inspired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses ARE to ERA. Erato is the Greek Muse of lyric and love poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is the Muse of lyric poetry, the goddess who inspired such poems.

clue.text: He made progress: this to smooth the way?

definitions.meaning: Hogarth's paintings A ... Progress follow a dissolute young man
a garden tool used to level gravel or soil

explanation.definitionFit: A rake is the libertine of Hogarth's series and also the toothed tool for levelling ground.

clue.text: Sour fruit alone turning stomach

indicators.note: turning stomach means only the middle of the word is turned round

parts.note: sole means single, alone

explanation.surface: A tart fruit eaten alone makes one queasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning stomach' reverses the middle two letters of SOLE, OL, to LO.
explanation.definitionFit: The sloe is the small, very sour fruit of the blackthorn, used for sloe gin.

clue.text: Face problems, and one can overcome any number

indicators.note: can overcome means the card word wraps round and holds the number

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards
N stands for an unspecified number in maths

explanation.surface: Facing trouble, but a single person can beat any odds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can overcome' puts the number inside the card, fitting the surface idea that an ace beats any numbered card.
explanation.definitionFit: Acne is a skin condition producing spots, chiefly on the face.

clue.text: Toy with dog and do cursory wash

parts.note: a top is a spinning toy
taken as written
to dog someone is to follow or tail them

explanation.surface: Playing with the dog then giving it a quick wash.
explanation.definitionFit: To top and tail is to wash just the face and bottom, as with a baby, a quick partial wash.

clue.text: Hear colleagues are numerous

indicators.note: hear signals the word is identified by its sound

parts.note: a team is a group of colleagues

explanation.surface: Listen to how many fellow workers there are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hear' says the word for colleagues is pronounced the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To teem is to be present in great quantities, to abound.

clue.text: Pay includes coin — grant that's not sufficient

indicators.note: includes means the pay word holds the others inside

parts.note: pay is income
P is a penny, a coin
to grant is to let or allow

explanation.surface: Wages that include a cash grant still don't add up to enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'includes' sets the coin and the grant inside the pay; 'that's' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something incomplete lacks parts, so it is not enough or insufficient.
